purpose: The candidate editorial configuration for production, set explicitly (plan E.X4, provisional; section 5.2, step 2). The code defaults are the pre-revision-6 configuration WIA rated 1 of 5. E.X4 confirms or reverts this after the held-out run and WIA's reviews. context.schedule.mining_live is true here (22 October, revision 8): the weekly learning loop categorises Gate 2 edits with models.context_mining, a paid call under a run plan, so apply this file at M4 step 5 together with the standing budget for the loop (a run plan covering stage context_mining); with no active plan the loop still runs, by rules, and says why. models.completion_tokens is 32000 (23 October, N2; it was 16000 from the M1 exit test). The cap is not a quality setting: a call is billed for what it writes, and the cap only sets the output reserve that a live weekly call is sized against and that a standing budget checks before sending (a call's worst case is its input plus this reserve). It is set so it never binds in normal work: on N2's paid run a brief's claim check of 126 statements used 8,601 reasoning tokens and was cut off at 16,000 (USD 0.25 spent for nothing), and its retry wrote 16,567. A reasoning model that still runs out, with no answer or with a structured answer cut off part way, is asked once more with a raised limit (E.B1). models.completion_tokens.moment_extraction is 32000 (23 October, N1 shakedown, from paid evidence): Luna's scene extractions used up to 20,607 output tokens, reasoning included, so the 16,000 of the other stages would cut a third of them off. N2 (23 October, the minimal gate, D40): every part of the new configuration passed its one-sample reading on the October delivery run and is named here: scene profile v3 (moments.extraction_profile and prompts.profile.extraction), strategist v7, card verification v4, brief contract v4 with writer v5. Knowledge base 9 (wia-kb-2026-10-22.c-a1a75795) passed its reading too and is recorded as the active version on the working copy (kb-benchmark), which N3 restores into production with the dump; it is not a setting here. A part WIA rejects in her live weeks is switched back by its key at no cost (D40). Content packs (Phase NP, D43, the owner, 24 October): features.packs on, the finisher and repair on Opus 5.5 (models.pack_writer) and the fidelity check on Sonnet 5.5 (models.pack_review), both at medium effort as in the planning probe, the pack-finish, pack-check and pack-repair v1 profiles, and packs.finish_mode finish; the switch-backs are models.pack_writer anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 (a third of the cost, little gain) and packs.finish_mode missing_only or assemble. A pack needs ATELIER_ALLOW_PACK_GENERATION=true on api and editorial-worker and the packs standing budget (D43f). NP-7 (26 October): the fidelity check is pack-check.v3 (the approved brief's WIA perspective among its sources; it caught both of the paid proof's missed clauses in its reading, research/n5-2026-10/), and the two person-started passes name their released profiles, pack-caption.v1 (the post-recording pass) and pack-refinish.v1 (finishing again with a permission). Writer v5.1 (NP.B10, 26 October) writes the brief's three Reels (story, stance, b-roll text); its free-model run and one paid brief with a blind reading passed (research/n5-2026-10/); v5 is the switch-back. N8 (25 October): strategist v8 (team-practice scenes, the identity records frozen with the cycle, founder notes named by their call), scene profile v4 (internal meetings recorded as team practice, D24) for both extraction keys, writer v5.2 (identities, what happened next from account memory, team-practice evidence marked) and internal meetings included (documents.included_call_types adds internal); each passed its free-model shakedown on copy C and its paid reading on copy D (research/n8-2026-10/README.md). The switch-backs are v7, v3, v5.1 and the five call types without internal. N6, N10 and N7 (25 October, the owner's decisions: research/n6-n11-2026-10/DECISIONS.md): the weekly cycle starts by itself every Sunday at 04:00 America/Chicago from 1 November 2026 (cycle.weekday 6, cycle.hour 4, cycle.schedule.enabled, cycle.schedule.first_day, cycle.schedule.actor: the shared WIA account, an approver and intake administrator), and an approved knowledge-base identity change is released by its approver without a paid benchmark (context.release.benchmark_required false). The switch-backs are cycle.schedule.enabled false (the cycle started from the app) and context.release.benchmark_required true. N11 (25 October): strategist v9 (one section, decisions and stakes belong in public: a counter-expected decision stays public with its figures left out, and the guardrail names the stakes the writer may state) passed the benchmark's reading on Week 2 beside v8's sample (research/n6-n11-2026-10/README.md); the switch-back is v8. Round 2 (27 October, WIA's feedback of 26 October): writer v5.3 (the central story and two premises of their own, the premises weighed, E2M's craft and editorial guide), finisher v3 (a plan, then the writing; an earlier brief's retold Reels replaced by premises of their own), check v4 (an editorial reading: what a prospect would infer, inherited work, lead quality, causation, slogans, overlapping premises, piece strength), repair v2 and refinish v2 (research/round2-2026-10/). The switch-backs are v5.2, pack-finish.v2, pack-check.v3, pack-repair.v1 and pack-refinish.v1. Round 2's second pass (27 October): finisher v4 and refinish v3 (the plan reads the card's whole call; Reels 2 and 3 are written and checked against the turns behind them); the switch-backs are pack-finish.v3 and pack-refinish.v2. No weekly spending caps (the owner, 27 October): budgets.uncapped is true, so no paid call is refused or waits for a cap; spend is still recorded. The costs page counts from the moment production was handed over (costs.count_from, the owner, 27 October): the team's own tests and remakes before it are left out of its totals, weeks and content packs.
